items.title: SAT imposes ₹1 lakh costs on MCX, quashes ₹1.5 crore penalty on Ventura Securities
items.summary: The Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) has imposed ₹1 lakh in costs on the Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX) for levying a ₹1.49 crore penalty on Ventura Securities Limited despite the maximum permissible penalty under a Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) circular being ₹2 lakh. [VSL Vs MCX] The tribunal also set aside the penalty order and directed MCX to immediately refund ₹1.76 crore, inclusive of GST, debited from Ventura's account. A Bench of Justice PS Dinesh Kumar (Presiding Officer), Meera Swarup (Technical Member) and Dr Dheeraj Bhatnagar (Technical Member) held that such conduct by an exchange functioning as a first-line regulator could not be countenanced. " Such act on the part of the respondent exchange, which is a first line regulator cannot be countenanced, " the SAT said. The dispute arose from an order dated September 28, 2026, passed by MCX's Member Committee imposing a penalty of ₹1.49 crore on Ventura Securities for allegedly violating client-level open position limits. items.title: ‘Love thy neighbour’: Karnataka HC refuses to quash cross-cases by neighbours over garbage disposal spat
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently refused to quash criminal cases filed by two neighbouring families against each other after a dispute about garbage disposal in their Bengaluru apartment complex escalated into physical violence [ Chandrashekhar Gupta v. State of Karnataka ]. Justice Suraj Govindaraj , on October 5, dismissed the petitions filed to quash the cases by Chandrashekhar Gupta and his wife, Neha Gupta, and their neighbours, Anant Gopal and his wife Swathi Sharma. The judge also emphasised that disagreements between neighbours must not escalate into physical violence. " The familiar exhortation, ‘Love thy neighbour’, embodies a principle of practical importance for peaceful coexistence ... The resort to physical violence is never an acceptable means of resolving a neighbourhood dispute ,” the Court said.
